fields.v: Spec-Driven AI (authors' own), version Not stated; two tools: SDLC Orchestrator and SDLC Context Platform (Pattern Manager, PatternOps dashboard)

Lifecycle artefacts generated by agents: product discovery notes, specifications (spec.md), design documents (design.md), implementation plans (plan.md), task lists (tasks.md), QA reports, review reports, traceability metadata, audit events, exportable artefact bundle. Governance artefacts: patterns (default, organization, project), baselines, golden examples, checklists. Context: structured JSON MCP payload (project profile, baseline, patterns, document chunks, files, graph context, adherence evidence, governance rules, quality gates)

Discovery, specification, design, planning, implementation support, testing, review, traceability/audit. Demonstration: register project and repository -> repository context rebuild (indexing, embeddings, graph import, adherence validation) -> manage and publish patterns/baselines -> orchestrator requests governed context for a task -> specialised agents generate spec.md, design.md, plan.md, tasks.md, QA and review reports -> human approval gates -> bundle export. Coding agents remain implementation executors

Human-in-the-loop gates in the orchestrator; human approval gates for irreversible or high-risk decisions; human review/approval of candidate patterns before publishing the baseline; bundle exported for review or audit
Not run as an evaluation; demonstration scenario of the tool (context preparation for a maintenance task) described and shown in a screencast

Not classifiable (closest: spec-anchored). The paper cites spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source for Spec Kit, Kiro and Tessl but does not classify its own framework; it describes specifications as 'verifiable contracts' and SDD specs as 'versioned, auditable, and executable sources of truth', and targets maintenance and evolution with traceability metadata

rev.why: 'Not stated' is not an allowed value. Versioned specs kept for maintenance with traceability suggest spec-anchored, but the paper never says whether spec.md is kept in sync with the code after the task, so 'not classifiable' is also defensible.
